comments.body:
here's a much more simplified version:
```
func.func @g2(%arg0: tensor<8xf32>, %arg1: tensor<8xi32>)
    -> (tensor<8xf32>, tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>) {
  %0:2 = iree_linalg_ext.sort dimension(0)
      outs(%arg0, %arg1 : tensor<8xf32>, tensor<8xi32>) {
  ^bb0(%a: f32, %b: f32, %c: i32, %d: i32):
    %lt = arith.cmpf olt, %a, %b : f32
    iree_linalg_ext.yield %lt : i1
  } -> tensor<8xf32>, tensor<8xi32>
  return %0#0, %0#1, %arg1 : tensor<8xf32>, tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>
}

```
--function=g2 --input="8xf32=8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1" --input="8xi32=10 11 12 13 14 15 16 17"
```
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
8xf32=1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
result[1]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=17 16 15 14 13 12 11 10
result[2]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=17 16 15 14 13 12 11 10 <---- this should be input 2
```

@devtbi i don't think result[2] should be input[2] since the op uses arg1 as outs it declares that it wants to write into arg1 in place, so %0#1 will alias %arg1. I'm also pretty sure this will happen for any linalg op that declares a function input as outs.

@ziereis can you explain why? I'd have thought arg1 is an SSA value. To my understanding, the outs are solely initial values for the output in tensor-land.

it's fine with linalg.generic:
```
iree-compile --iree-hal-target-device=local --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends="llvm-cpu" dps_control.mlir -o=dps.vmfb
ree-run-module --module=dps.vmfb --function=dps_control --device=local-sync --input=8xi32=1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8


func.func @dps_control(%arg0: tensor<8xi32>) -> (tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>) {
  %c1 = arith.constant 1 : i32
  %0 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],
                       iterator_types = ["parallel"]}
      outs(%arg0 : tensor<8xi32>) {
  ^bb0(%o: i32):
    %r = arith.addi %o, %c1 : i32
    linalg.yield %r : i32
  } -> tensor<8xi32>
  return %0, %arg0 : tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>
}

EXEC @dps_control
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9
result[1]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
```

@devtbi Okay i took another look at the IR for your initial snipped for the sort and you are right result[2] should be (regardless of whether %arg1 should be written to in-place) still return the values of %arg1. <del>What i would have expected to happen is that bufferization would create a new allocation, copy %arg1 into this allocation, do the sort in-place into the buffer of %arg1 and still return the copy of %arg1 as result[2]. (i think this is what would happen if hal.tensor.alias is used on the result of the generic + the arg) </del>

edit: i tried checking the semantics of hal.tensor.alias and the "copy-on-write" semantic i though would be happening are explicitly stated not to happen. My bad! 

ref: https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/HAL/#haltensoralias-haltensoraliasop
> Explicit aliasing side-steps any analysis that may be performed by the compiler and requires users to guarantee that the safety of the aliasing. Copy-on-write, alias analysis for overlap detection, and ordering via use-def chains are all ignorant of the aliased buffer memory and only ensure the compiler consumes or produces the aliased memory consistent with itself.

However i think you are right, without any extra hint it should not write into %arg1 and should behave like the second snippet you have shown. Interestingly i have been using linalg_ext.scatter which is buggy in the same way as the sort, thats why i kind of though this is the expected behavior :D but you are right its not. 

```
iree-run-module --module=scatter_control.vmfb --device=local-task --function=scatter_control --input="8xi32=[0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7]" --input="3xi32=[100 200 300]" --input="3x1xi32=[1 3 5]"
```

```mlir
func.func @scatter_control(%original: tensor<8xi32>,
                           %updates: tensor<3xi32>,
                           %indices: tensor<3x1xi32>)
    -> (tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>) {
  %0 = iree_linalg_ext.scatter
      dimension_map = [0]
      unique_indices(true)
      ins(%updates, %indices : tensor<3xi32>, tensor<3x1xi32>)
      outs(%original : tensor<8xi32>) {
  ^bb0(%update: i32, %orig: i32):
    iree_linalg_ext.yield %update : i32
  } -> tensor<8xi32>
  return %0, %original : tensor<8xi32>, tensor<8xi32>
}
```

result:

```
EXEC @scatter_control
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=0 100 2 200 4 300 6 7
result[1]: hal.buffer_view
8xi32=0 100 2 200 4 300 6 7
```
